title: Built-in test recognition takes `bash w.sh -c 'cargo test'` as a cargo test: engram_unwrap_shell_command accepts any words before the -c flag
outcome: A shell-wrapper line is recognised as a built-in test only when the wrapper itself runs the script: words before the script flag that make the shell run something else (a script file, `-File`, chained commands) are not read as a wrapper.
acceptance: `bash w.sh -c 'cargo test'`, `pwsh -File w.ps1 -Command 'cargo test'` and `bash --version ; true -c 'cargo test'` are not recognised as cargo test checks, each with a control that fails before the change.

Ordinary built-in wrappers that the recognition takes today (for example `bash -lc 'cargo test'` and `pwsh -Command cargo test`) keep their recognition and fingerprint unchanged, shown by the existing recognition tests passing unchanged.
